title: I wish...
theme: Wishes expanded (I wish + would, would rather, it's time + past, if only)
goal: Student expresses desire about others' actions, preferences, and urgent recommendations using subjunctive structures beyond basic wishes.
connects_to: M21 (Phrasal verbs avançados) — shift to lexical density.
module_chunks: I wish you would + base (complaint about behavior)
If only + past simple / past perfect

units.title: I wish you would
units.grammar_focus: I wish + would + base (annoyance/desire about another's recurring action)
units.real_life_context: You express a wish that someone else would change their behavior.

grammar.sentence: I wish you _____ stop interrupting me!
grammar.explanation: "I wish + would + base" to complain about another person's recurring behavior. "Would stop" — a wish for them to stop.

grammar.sentence: I wish she _____ listen to me.
grammar.explanation: Wish + would expresses a wish about another person's future/recurring action. Not used for yourself (use wish + past for that).

grammar.sentence: I wish people _____ smoke in restaurants.
grammar.explanation: "Wouldn't smoke" — negative wish. General complaint about others' behavior.

grammar.sentence: I wish it _____ raining!
grammar.explanation: "I wish it would stop raining" — wish + would for a desired change. Events/weather also work.

grammar.sentence: I wish you _____ be quiet for one minute.
grammar.explanation: "I wish you would be quiet" — wish for a specific action. Annoyed tone.

grammar.sentence: I wish my neighbors _____ make so much noise.
grammar.explanation: "Wouldn't make noise" — ongoing complaint. Standard negative.

grammar.sentence: I wish he _____ stop complaining.
grammar.explanation: "Would stop complaining" — wish for them to stop the recurring behavior.

grammar.sentence: I wish you will listen to me.
grammar.answer: I wish you would listen to me.
grammar.explanation: "Will" doesn't combine with wish. For wishes about others' future/behavior, use "would".

grammar.sentence: I wish I would be taller.
grammar.hint: Para EU mesmo, use wish + past simple
grammar.explanation: "Wish + would" is NOT used for yourself. For yourself, use wish + past simple ("I wish I were"). Wish + would is only for OTHERS.

grammar.passage: I wish you would stop interrupting me. I wish she would listen to me. I wish people wouldn't smoke in restaurants. I wish it would stop raining. I wish my neighbors wouldn't make so much noise.
grammar.question: What does the speaker wish about restaurants?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I wish people wouldn't smoke in restaurants".

listening_speaking.text: I wish you would stop interrupting.
I wish she would listen to me.
I wish it would stop raining.

units.title: If only
units.grammar_focus: "If only" + past simple (present regret) and + past perfect (past regret)
units.real_life_context: You express stronger or more dramatic regret than "I wish" with "if only".

grammar.sentence: If only I _____ more time!
grammar.explanation: "If only + past simple" for PRESENT regret. Same pattern as "I wish I had" but with a more emphatic/dramatic tone.

grammar.sentence: If only I _____ studied harder!
grammar.explanation: "If only + past perfect" for regret about the PAST. "If only I had studied" — same pattern as "I wish I had studied".

grammar.sentence: If only she _____ here right now.
grammar.explanation: "If only she were here" — present wish. "Were" for all persons in wish/if only.

grammar.sentence: If only we _____ left earlier!
grammar.explanation: "If only we had left" — past regret. Standard past perfect.

grammar.sentence: If only I _____ speak more languages!
grammar.explanation: "If only I could" — present ability wish. "Could" + base.

grammar.sentence: If only he _____ listened to me!
grammar.explanation: "If only he had listened" — dramatic past regret.

grammar.sentence: If only the rain _____ stop!
grammar.explanation: "If only it would stop" — wish about future/behavior. Similar to wish + would.

grammar.sentence: If only I have more time!
grammar.answer: If only I had more time!
grammar.explanation: "Have" doesn't work with if only for a present wish. The standard is "if only + past simple" for the present.

grammar.sentence: If only I would have studied!
grammar.explanation: "Would have" doesn't fit in if only. For the past, use past perfect ("had studied"). Same rule as wish.

grammar.passage: If only I had more time! If only I had studied harder! If only she were here now. If only we had left earlier! If only the rain would stop!
grammar.question: What does the speaker wish about studying?
grammar.explanation: The text says "If only I had studied harder!".

units.title: I'd rather
units.grammar_focus: Would rather + base (own preference) and would rather + past simple (about another)
units.real_life_context: You state preferences politely or express what you'd prefer someone else to do.

grammar.sentence: I _____ stay home tonight.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather + base" for your own preference. Standard structure: "would rather + base form".

grammar.sentence: I'd rather _____ pizza than sushi.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather + base form". "Rather have pizza" — base form without "to".

grammar.sentence: I'd rather you _____ smoke here.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather + person + past simple" for preference about another person. "Didn't smoke" — negative past simple.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather _____ stay than go out.
grammar.explanation: Negative: "I'd rather NOT + base". "Not stay" — negative preference.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather _____ coffee than tea.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather drink coffee" — simple preference with base form.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather you _____ to me before deciding.
grammar.explanation: "I'd rather you talked" — preference about the other person's behavior. Past simple, not base form.

grammar.sentence: She'd rather _____ outside on the patio.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather sit outside" — own preference, base form.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather to go home.
grammar.explanation: "Would rather" + base form directly, without "to". "Rather to go" doesn't exist.

grammar.sentence: I'd rather you stop talking.
grammar.explanation: When it's about ANOTHER person, use past simple ("stopped"). "Stop" without -ed would only work as a direct command, not a preference.

grammar.passage: I'd rather stay home tonight. I'd rather have pizza than sushi. I'd rather you didn't smoke here. I'd rather not go out today. I'd rather you talked to me before deciding.
grammar.question: What would the speaker rather have for dinner?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I'd rather have pizza than sushi".

units.title: It's time
units.real_life_context: You urge someone to do something they should have already done.

grammar.sentence: It's time we _____.
grammar.explanation: "It's time + past simple" expressa urgência. "It's time we left" = é hora de sairmos (já passamos do momento ideal).

grammar.sentence: It's high time you _____ a decision.
grammar.explanation: "It's high time + past simple" — versão mais enfática. "It's high time" indica que está MUITO atrasado.

grammar.sentence: It's about time you _____ to bed.
grammar.explanation: "It's about time" — quase sinônimo de "it's high time", também urgente. + past simple.

grammar.sentence: It's time we _____ this seriously.
grammar.explanation: "It's time we took" — sugestão urgente. Past simple.

grammar.sentence: It's high time you _____ a real vacation.
grammar.explanation: "It's high time you had a vacation" — urgência enfática.

grammar.sentence: It's about time he _____ growing up.
grammar.explanation: "It's about time he started growing up" — emphatic suggestion about someone.

grammar.sentence: It's time we _____ honest with each other.
grammar.explanation: "It's time we were honest" — past simple "were" (universal subjuntivo). Não "are".

grammar.sentence: It's time we leave.
grammar.explanation: "It's time" doesn't take present simple directly. Always past simple ("left").

grammar.sentence: It's high time you will make a decision.
grammar.answer: It's high time you made a decision.
grammar.explanation: "Will" doesn't fit. The pattern is "it's high time + past simple" ("made").

grammar.passage: It's time we left for the airport. It's high time you made a decision. It's about time you went to bed. It's time we took this seriously.
grammar.question: What should you go to?
grammar.explanation: The text says "It's about time you went to bed".

units.title: Mixed wishes and preferences

grammar.explanation: If only + past simple for a present wish.

grammar.explanation: "I'd rather not + base" — negative preference.

grammar.explanation: "It's time + past simple" — urgency.

grammar.explanation: "I'd rather you + past simple" for preference about the other person.

grammar.sentence: If only she _____ understand me!
grammar.explanation: "If only + would" for a behavioral change.

grammar.sentence: It's high time you _____ a real job.
grammar.explanation: "It's high time + past simple" — emphatic urgency.

grammar.sentence: I wish you will be quiet.
grammar.answer: I wish you would be quiet.
grammar.explanation: "Will" doesn't fit in wish. For future/behavior, use "would".

grammar.sentence: It's time we leave.
